title: Access boundary matrix and admin escape clauses
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Summary:
Design a pragmatic RBAC v2 role model expressed as an access boundary matrix that maps resource families -> scopes -> canonical permissions, with explicit 'admin escape' clauses (breakglass/elevation rules) and audit instrumentation hooks. This ticket drives the concrete data model, runtime evaluation behavior, SSO/SAML mapping guidance, and a staged migration plan for existing roles.

Goals:
- Produce a deterministic, explainable permission resolution algorithm for multi-tenant resources (projects, datasets, models, deployments).
- Define a compact yet expressive role and scope vocabulary so product teams can declare least-privilege roles without combinatorial explosion.
- Model admin escape semantics: temporary elevation, emergency responders, and constrained breakglass flows that leave immutable audit traces.
- Ensure audit logging is complete and actionable (actor, resolved policy, resource snapshot, justification token).
- Define SSO/SAML claim-to-role mapping recommendations and provisioning guidance for IdP teams.

Design proposals (high level):
1) Access boundary matrix (ABM): a three-column canonical table: ResourceFamily, Scope (e.g., project:read, model:write), CanonicalPermissions (create/read/update/delete, manage-rollout, bind-roles). Each row represents a smallest-grain permission set that runtime can evaluate quickly. We will publish ABM as a human-readable and machine-consumable CSV/JSON artifact in the repo.

2) Role model primitives:
- Role: set of ABM rows + metadata (immutable id, version).
- RoleBinding: (principal, role, resource_anchor, metadata). Resource_anchor supports: tenant, project, resource-id, or global.
- TemporalBinding: RoleBinding with expiry + optional justification token.

3) Policy evaluation order (deterministic):
- Collect principal's bindings (explicit and inherited).
- Apply deny rules first (explicit deny list).
- Aggregate allowed ABM rows; compute effective permission set.
- Short-circuit: emergency-breakglass tokens (signed) may temporarily add a RoleBinding but must be recorded and require a privileged release step.

4) Admin escape clauses (breakglass):
- Two-tier escape: 1) Emergency Responders (tight-scope, time-limited elevation) 2) Incident Admin Mode (session-unlocked window with MFA and justification).
- Both require a signed justification token with metadata: initiator, incident id, TTL, approval path (if applicable).
- Tokens must be verifiable by runtime using KMS/HSM-signed claims to prevent forgery.
- Automatic revocation hook: tokens expire and are revocable from Console and API; revocations are streamed to evaluation layer.

5) Audit schema (required fields):
- event_id, timestamp, actor_principal, actor_identity_source (SSO|API_KEY), resolved_roles (list), resolved_permissions (list), resource_snapshot (resource id + metadata hash), decision (allow|deny), request_trace_id, justification_token_id (if applicable), evaluation_latency_ms, policy_version.
- Logs must be append-only and forwarded to SIEM; retention policy will be configured by deployments.

SSO/SAML mapping guidance:
- Two mapping modalities: push-based (IdP SAML assertion contains groups/roles) and pull-based (SCIM provisioning into Directory).
- Recommend canonical claim names: redwood_role, redwood_department, redwood_project_affinity. For SAML, map SAML attribute redwood_role -> RoleBinding on first sign-in; include metadata to auto-provision TemporalBindings with short TTL for contractor groups.
- For enterprise customers using SCIM, provide an IdP-to-RoleBinder tool that ingests group membership and translates to RoleBindings using configurable templates.

Migration plan (staged):
- Phase 0: Define ABM and canonical permission names; publish docs and examples.
- Phase 1: Implement evaluation engine changes behind feature-flag; create compatibility layer that translates old role names to new Roles (one-to-one mapping file).
- Phase 2: Run dual-eval: runtime computes both legacy and v2 results and emits diffs to a migration dashboard (no enforcement change).
- Phase 3: Address diffs, update bindings, and flip flag for enforcement for low-risk tenants.
- Phase 4: Provide self-serve migration tooling and a rollback path.

Acceptance criteria (must pass):
- ABM JSON schema and canonical CSV exist in the repo.
- Runtime can evaluate ABM rows under feature-flag with performance within 10% of current RBAC.
- Breakglass flow implemented end-to-end with signed justification tokens and audit entries visible in Console.
- SAML/SCIM mapping docs and a sample IdP configuration shipped.
- Migration dashboard shows role-diff for at least 3 pilot tenants and provides actionable recommendations.

Tradeoffs and open questions:
- Granularity vs cognitive load: fine-grained ABM increases correctness but may require role composition tooling. We'll prototype role templates.
- Deny vs implicit deny: prefer explicit deny semantics for critical admin actions (destructive ops) but must avoid accidental lockouts. We need a simulated guardrail system.
- Storage: RoleBinding store needs low-latency reads; evaluate Redis vs strongly-consistent KV store (consistency required for admin escapes).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Breakglass abuse. Mitigation: short TTL, secondary approver where available, SIEM alerting and automatic post-mortem ticket creation.
- Risk: Migration causing permission regressions. Mitigation: dual-eval, diffs, and conservative rollout with opt-out for enterprise tenants.

Next steps (owners and timeline):

- Security review and threat modeling: owner: Priya Menon. (Due 2026-03-18)
- Console work: UX for breakglass prompts + audit timeline: owner: Sara O'Neill (PM) - separate ticket.
